family.description: NfeD-like proteins are widely distributed throughout prokaryotes and are frequently associated with genes encoding stomatin-like proteins (slipins). There appear to be three major groups: an ancestral group with only an N-terminal serine protease domain and this C-terminal beta sheet-rich domain which is structurally very similar to the OB-fold domain, associated with its neighbouring slipin cluster; a second major group with an additional middle, membrane-spanning domain, associated in some species with eoslipin and in others with yqfA; a final 'artificial' group which unites truncated forms lacking the protease region and associated with their ancestral gene partner, either yqfA or eoslipin. This NefD, C-terminal, domain appears to be the major one for relating to the associated protein. NfeD homologues are clearly reliant on their conserved gene neighbour which is assumed to be necessary for function, either through direct physical interaction or by functioning in the same pathway, possibly involve with lipid-rafts [[cite:PUB00064250]].

causal_graphs.context: Chiba2006 Figure2A/B text and legend. L medium with 1mM IPTG; 3-ul serial-dilution plate spots at 42C for 24h, and a separate liquid-growth time course shifted from 30C to 42C. Plate comparisons at 30C for 17h and with 0.4% glucose provide conditional controls.

evidence.explanation: Functional interaction Results, Figure2A legend and strain/plasmid Methods; text-supported direction, not a visually quantified image or YbbJ-only rescue.

edges.mechanism: Adding ybbJ to the QmcA expression construct improves the reported colony-growth suppression of the ftsH/htpX defect under induction; the cellular mediator is unresolved.
edges.subject: pair

evidence.explanation: Figure2B legend and corresponding Results; same AD1762/sfhC21 background, pSTD622 versus pSTD620, not ordinary wild-type thermotolerance.

edges.mechanism: The joint expression construct improves reported liquid growth relative to qmcA-only cells following the temperature shift, without identifying a direct protein-quality-control reaction.
edges.subject: pair

causal_graphs.family_mapping: MC4100-derived YbbJ clone; current reference P0AAS3 v2 is 152 aa with PF01957 94-148. The reference sequence changed in 2007 and is not a verified historical plasmid sequence. QmcA is a required coexpressed partner, not a second PF01957 protein.
causal_graphs.limitations: YbbJ alone did not suppress. Similar QmcA abundance was reported without shown data. No isolated PF01957 activity, direct chaperoning, proteolysis or FtsH activation is established. The source images, replicate counts and exact effect sizes remain uninspected; graphs retain text-supported direction only. Liquid and plate readouts are not sequential steps.

causal_graphs.context: Butcher2006 Figure4A text and legend, Table3 and spot-on-lawn Methods; 0.7% LB agar, 100ul lawn OD600 0.4 in 2ml agar, 2ul producer OD600 0.6, overnight37C.

evidence.explanation: Figure4A column4 and associated Results; the ledger records the native whole-operon genotype and matched controls, not a single-domain intervention.

edges.mechanism: Removing the three-gene locus increases the reported growth-inhibition zone in this immunity-deficient lawn; the responsible molecular contribution of YqeZ is not isolated.
edges.subject: operon_loss

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The jointly deleted operon contains YqeZ/NfeD1, current B. subtilis 168 reference P54465 v1, 437 aa, PF01957 382-435. CU1065 is the experimental strain, not the reference accession's exact verified allele. YqfA and YqfB are not independently attributed to PF01957.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole-operon perturbation cannot isolate YqeZ or its domain. YqfB-only deletion is similarly sensitive. Producer sunA deletion and SPbeta restoration remove inhibition, but no purified-peptide MIC or degradation assay was performed in this comparison. Original Figure4/supplements and quantitative replication remain uninspected; only the text-supported qualitative direction is retained.

causal_graphs.scope: B. subtilis CU1065 without SPbeta immunity; HB5331 yqeZyqfAB::kan versus the parent lawn, exposed to JH642 producer.
causal_graphs.title: Deleting the YqeZ-containing operon increases sublancin-associated inhibition

causal_graphs.context: Butcher2006 Figure4B column3 and Methods; 20mM xylose induction, 0.7% LB agar, JH642 producer, overnight37C. pSG1 single-crossover integration was PCR-confirmed; this is not deletion/rescue in HB5331.

evidence.explanation: Figure4B legend/Results and complementation Methods; whole-operon expression, matched20mM xylose and separate sigW background.

edges.mechanism: Expression of the complete operon bypasses part of the missing sigma-factor-dependent resistance in the reported assay; it does not resolve which biochemical activity mediates protection.
edges.subject: induced_operon

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The entire operon includes YqeZ, reference P54465 v1 with PF01957 382-435. Neither isolated YqeZ nor its PF01957 domain was shown sufficient. The study reports a YqfB V65E reference difference in CU1065/JH642, not a YqeZ mutation.
causal_graphs.limitations: Xylose itself reduces inhibition zones, so unmatched induced/uninduced comparisons would confound the effect. Partial yqfAB or yqfB constructs failed to complement but do not demonstrate YqeZ-only sufficiency. No direct peptide cleavage, independent domain action or complete restoration magnitude is assigned; original figures/supplements remain uninspected.

causal_graphs.title: Induced YqeZ-containing operon reduces inhibition in a sigW mutant
